title: Multiplying Larger Numbers By One-Digit Numbers: Finding Missing Digits

key_prerequisites.name: Three- and Four-Digit by One-Digit Multiplication

sections.normalized_html:
From left to right, what are the missing digits in the following multiplication problem?

[MATH: _(5)|_(0)|_(0)|_(3); 7|9|0|0|6; ×|6; [math]\phantom{4}[/math]|[math]\phantom{7}[/math]|4|[math]\phantom{0}[/math]|3|6]

From left to right, what are the missing digits in the following multiplication problem?

[MATH: _(5)|_(0)|_(0)|_(3); 7|9|0|0|6; ×|6; [math]\phantom{4}[/math]|[math]\phantom{7}[/math]|4|[math]\phantom{0}[/math]|3|6]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we multiply the ones:

[MATH: _(3); 7|9|0|0|6; ×|6; 6|6 × 6 = 36; Carry:3; Write:6]

Next, we multiply the tens:

[MATH: _(0)|_(3); 7|9|0|0|6; ×|6; 3|6|0 × 6 = 0and3 + 0 = 3; Carry:0; Write:3]

Next, we multiply the hundreds:

[MATH: _(0)|_(0)|_(3); 7|9|0|0|6; ×|6; 0|3|6|0 × 6 = 0and0 + 0 = 0; Carry:0; Write:0]

Next, we multiply the thousands:

[MATH: _(5)|_(0)|_(0)|_(3); 7|9|0|0|6; ×|6; 4|0|3|6|9 × 6 = 54and0 + 54 = 54; Carry:5; Write:4]

Finally, we multiply the tens of thousands:

[MATH: _(5)|_(0)|_(0)|_(3); 7|9|0|0|6; ×|6; [math]\color{red}4[/math]|[math]\color{red}7[/math]|4|0|3|6|7 × 6 = 42and5 + 42 = 47; Carry:−; Write:47]

Therefore, the missing digits, from left-to-right, are [MATH: \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}4},\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}7},] and [MATH: \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}0}.]
